newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Philips confident consumer products upturn durable.
newsitem.headline: Philips confident consumer products upturn durable.

text.p: Philips Electronics NV said on Wednesday it was confident that its previously loss-making consumer products unit was on track to provide sustainable, profitable growth.

Philips earlier today said first quarter net from normal operations rose 22 percent to 460 million guilders ($239 million), with the consumer products unit turning in an operating profit of 206 million guilders against a previous 52 million loss.
The unit has historically been weighed down by losses from Philips' German affiliate Grundig, but from the beginning of 1997 Philips stopped absorbing 100 percent of Grundig's losses.

Philips said it was also beginning to reap the benefits of last year's 800 million guilder pre-tax extraordinary charge to restructure the Sound & Vision unit which forms the heart of its consumer products business.

"We are very pleased that after a hell of a lot of work -- that's not finished by any means, one swallow doesn't make a summer -- they have demonstrated to themselves and (to) the outside world that they can make money at their business," Philips vice chairman Dudley Eustace told a news conference.
"They are profitable and they are cash positive and those two are fundamental to a healthy future," he said.
Eustace said the fundamental changes being made in Sound & Vision, how it managed its technical and logistical development, would be lasting.
"The benefits of the purchasing program, the cost-reduction program have shown through, whereby Sound & Vision has been able to outrun the price pressure by lower costs," he said.
"I have some confidence that this team has already made its mark on a more permanent basis, in creating a sustainable, profitable business," Eustace told reporters.
Share analysts welcomed the results with a move to upgrade earnings forecasts for the year, with some agreeing the outlook appeared brighter as restructuring benefits filtered through.

"These results are outstanding. I think we will see more improvement in consumer electronics in the rest of this year and also in the first half of 1998," said Frits de Vries analyst at Theodoor Gilissen Bankiers.
He said the cost savings currently achieved with the restructurings at Sounds & Vision should be sufficient to guarantee further improvements.

Susan Anthony, a London-based analyst with Schroders, said the consumer products division's performance was about 100 million guilders above estimates and clearly showed the benefits of restructuring, but she warned against excessive optimism.

"All quarterly results will inevitably look good on a year-to-year comparison, but we have to look at the underlying performance....There were some points that performed somewhat worse than expected...Is there going to be another restructuring programme at some later stage?," she asked.
